name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
role: Italian general and revolutionary, leader of the Expedition of the Thousand (1860) and Italian unification
summary: Garibaldi was a republican-minded nationalist and volunteer commander who fought for Italian unity and for liberal and republican causes in South America, Rome, Sicily, Poland-adjacent campaigns and France. He accepted Savoy monarchy as the means to unity, exercised a short dictatorship in Sicily and Naples, and was fiercely anticlerical, hostile to the temporal power of the papacy, and sympathetic to the International and later to peace and arbitration among free democracies.

notes: Searched all themes, including his decrees as dictator (taxes, land, asylums, Jesuits) and the memoirs. Sources and local corpus available were thin on economy, ecology, technology, gender and most government detail, so those stay null. His mature position on monarchy versus republic is mixed: he accepted the Savoy king in 1860 but remained republican in sympathy. Late League of Democracy items (death-penalty abolition, women's emancipation, standing army) rest only on secondary web pages I could not verify, so they are not used. His 1867 and later words on war and peace are not used where his campaigns give a record.
